# Findings: 1.1 Configuration and root discovery

Reviewed: 894dd6687736..5f6d8ad278f3, 5 files. Steps: all done.

## F1 — Wrong-case keys bypass the unknown-key check, and `Kinds` is silently replaced by the defaults

- Class: gap
- Confidence: high
- Where: `internal/config/config.go:40`, `internal/config/config.go:50`
- Situation: `.benchpress.toml` uses a key that differs only in case from a Go
  field name, e.g. `Kinds = ["x"]`, `Dir = "work"`, or `AREAS = ["maps"]`.
- Happens: BurntSushi's decoder matches those keys to the fields
  case-insensitively, so they are not in `meta.Undecoded()` and no unknown-key
  error is returned. For `Kinds` the value is then lost as well:
  `meta.IsDefined("kinds")` is false because the mapping key is `"Kinds"`, so
  `Load` overwrites the configured list with `DefaultKinds`. A reproduced run
  of `Load` on `Kinds = ["x"]` returned `Kinds:[bug change design idea]` with a
  nil error. `Dir` and `AREAS` are likewise accepted under the wrong case.
- Should: only the exact keys `dir`, `kinds` and `areas` are known; any other
  key is an error naming it, per `docs/DESIGN.md` §2 ("An unknown key is an
  error, so a misspelt key is not silently ignored"). Since `Undecoded` does not
  cover this, validate the top-level names in `meta.Keys()` against the allowed
  set instead.
- Test: none exists; add a case-variant key (at least `Kinds = ["x"]`) that must
  fail `Load`.

## F2 — `FindRoot` treats a directory named `.benchpress.toml` as the config file

- Class: gap
- Confidence: medium
- Where: `internal/config/config.go:63`
- Situation: a directory named `.benchpress.toml` sits at or below the real
  config file, for example `root/.benchpress.toml` (a file) and
  `root/mid/.benchpress.toml/` (a directory), with `FindRoot` called from
  `root/mid/a`.
- Happens: `os.Stat` succeeds for the directory, so `FindRoot` returns `mid` as
  the root; the real config at `root` is shadowed and never found. With no file
  above, `Load` then fails with `read .../.benchpress.toml: is a directory`
  rather than returning `ErrNoRoot`. Both cases reproduced.
- Should: only a directory that holds a regular file named `.benchpress.toml`
  counts as the root; a directory with that name is not the file, so the walk
  should continue upward, per the unit goal and `docs/DESIGN.md` §2 ("the first
  directory holding `.benchpress.toml`").
- Test: none exists; add a test with a `.benchpress.toml` directory below a
  real config file.

Reviewed: 4a4b5d337e43..96d29ded5a23, 2 files. Steps: all done.

## F1 — Appending a field to a CRLF file whose closing `---` has no newline inserts an LF line

- Class: slip
- Confidence: high
- Where: `internal/topic/topic.go:179`, `internal/topic/topic.go:181`
- Situation: a CRLF topic whose closing `---` is the last line and has no
  trailing newline, e.g. `"---\r\nkind: bug\r\narea: maps\r\nstate: open\r\n---"`,
  and `Set(src, "plan", "docs/plans/x.md")`.
- Happens: the new field takes the closing line's terminator, which is empty,
  so the fallback is a bare LF: the output is
  `"---\r\nkind: bug\r\narea: maps\r\nstate: open\r\nplan: docs/plans/x.md\n---"`.
  The existing bytes are kept, but the file is left with mixed CRLF/LF endings.
  The same happens with an empty CRLF front matter ending `---` without a
  newline. `TestSetAppendCRLF` does not catch it because its closing `---`
  already ends in `\r\n`.
- Should: keep the file's CRLF style for the appended line, as the work order's
  "CRLF input left CRLF" requires and the handover claims ("`Set` appends with
  the closing `---`'s terminator, so CRLF files stay CRLF"). When the closing
  line has no terminator, use the preceding line's terminator (and only fall
  back to `\n` when the file has no line ending at all).
- Test: none exists; add a `Set` append case whose closing `---` has no final
  newline and that expects `\r\n` before the closing line.

## F2 — Image syntax is reported as a topic link

- Class: design
- Confidence: medium
- Where: `internal/topic/topic.go:373` (the `[` case in `collectLinks`)
- Situation: a body containing an image, e.g. `![screenshot](img/shot.png)`.
- Happens: the `!` falls through the `default` arm, the following `[` is parsed
  by `parseLink`, and the image target is appended to `Topic.Links`. `lint`
  then applies the `link`/`topic-link` rules to it, so a missing image file
  outside `dir` is reported as a broken relative link, and an image target
  ending in `.md` inside `dir` would be reported as a missing topic.
- Should: the work order asks for inline Markdown links `[text](target)` and
  `[text](target "title")`; an image is not a link. `docs/DESIGN.md` §3's
  *Links* paragraph likewise says topics link to each other. Skip a `[` that is
  immediately preceded by `!` (the handover lists this as an open problem; it
  is still a false positive for the `link` rule).
- Test: none exists; add a case with `![alt](missing.png)` and expect no link
  (or, if images are to count, make that a design decision and test it).

## F3 — An empty level-one heading (`#`) is accepted as the topic title

- Class: slip
- Confidence: medium
- Where: `internal/topic/topic.go:317`
- Situation: a topic whose first non-blank body line is `#` (or `#` followed
  only by spaces), e.g. `"---\nkind: bug\narea: maps\nstate: open\n---\n\n#\n"`.
- Happens: `heading1` returns `("", true)` for a line that trims to `#`, so
  `Parse` sets `Title` to the empty string, `TitleLine` to 7, and reports no
  `title` issue. A topic with no title text therefore passes the structural
  checks, and `ls`/the board show an empty title.
- Should: `docs/DESIGN.md` §3 says the first non-blank line is "a level-one
  heading, `# Title`"; a bare `#` has no title, so it should be reported as a
  `title` issue rather than accepted as an empty one.
- Test: none exists; add a `Parse` case with a bare `#` and expect a `title`
  issue (and no empty `Title`).
